semantic_anchor: one shared memory rule, feedback through repeated reads, and the difference between multiplying one route and adding a shared weight's uses
prompt: Create a clean handwritten teaching page titled 'Why old feedback fades or grows'. The image is ONLY a flat, front-facing, pale ivory ruled notepad page, filling the frame edge to edge. Thin very light blue horizontal rules and one faint red left margin. No photographic surroundings. Handwrite with highly legible dark navy ballpoint-style ink: natural slightly irregular upright student handwriting, not cursive calligraphy or printed typesetting. Leave generous space between six short numbered groups. Small restrained orange circles highlight repeated w factors; blue underlining marks the backward message. This redraws the idea of a handwritten RNN note, but correct notation matters more than copying a photograph. Put these exact ideas on the page, in this order, with no extra derivations: 1. 'Read a note, update the memory' then h_t = w h_(t-1) + x_t. Below: 'Same w at every read. x is the current note's fixed write.' Draw three small memory cards linked by arrows marked w, to make repeated use visible. 2. 'A wrong ending sends teaching feedback back' then a simple line 'last memory -> note head -> guess -> ending error L'. 3. 'How would changing w change the error?' then dL/dw = (dL/dh_T) (dh_T/dw). Under the first factor write 'feedback from the ending'; under the second write 'how w affected the memory'. 4. 'Current use + earlier uses' then dh_t/dw = h_(t-1) + w (dh_(t-1)/dw). Next line: dh_T/dw = h_(T-1) + w h_(T-2) + w^2 h_(T-3) + ... . Use proper handwritten subscripts and exponents, not literal underscores. 5. Draw a thin orange box around 'One old-state route: dh_T/dh_(T-k) = w^k'. Beneath write 'A route multiplies the links. The full weight feedback adds all its uses.' 6. In large readable handwriting: '|w| < 1: the old message fades'; '|w| = 1: this linear route keeps its size'; '|w| > 1: the old message can grow'. Footer: 'One-number linear microscope. Real RNNs also have a squash response.' All formulas must be correctly indexed, with capital T for the ending and k for the number of handoffs. Do not include an incorrect final w^k h_(T-k) term. Do not add a mean-squared-error derivation, probability arrays, softmax expansion, or numerical worked example. The page should feel like a concise, carefully written personal note, not a dense mathematical poster.
acceptance_criteria: 1152 by 1536 portrait ruled notepad only; no human thumb, hand, pen, desk, window, dark scene or surrounding background. All required handwriting is readable at notebook width. Correct recurrence, chain-rule factors, shared-weight recurrence and old-state path gain; explicitly distinguish the sum over shared uses from a single w^k route. No invented measurements. Main takeaway is repeated weakening or amplification of teaching feedback, not arithmetic.
prohibited_content: People, hands, thumbs, fingers, faces, arms, pens, desk or table, room, keyboard, window, photographic background, roll of paper, logos, watermarks, provider names, unreadable cursive, tiny dense type, fabricated numbers, training curves, extra algebra, wrong subscripts, or a claim that every real RNN's entire gradient is determined solely by |w|.
alt_text: A clean handwritten notepad explains a scalar linear RNN: one shared memory rule is reused at each read; the ending error supplies backward feedback; shared-weight feedback adds its uses, while one earlier-state route crosses k multipliers and has gain w to the power k. The page distinguishes fading, steady and growing linear routes and notes that real RNNs also have a squash response.

semantic_anchor: substitute each chosen memory weight into the same backward-feedback formula, showing repeated factors before their fading, steady or growing results
prompt: Create a clean handwritten teaching notepad page on pale ivory paper with light blue horizontal rules, a faint red left margin, and natural highly legible upright dark navy ballpoint handwriting. The entire image is the flat front-facing page, with no hand or surrounding scene. Landscape 3:2. Title: 'Plug the weight into every backward link'. First explain in plain English: 'Start with 1 unit of ending feedback. Each link multiplies it by the same w.' Below that write the main formula prominently: 'earlier feedback = ending feedback x w^k'. Immediately beneath, a smaller but legible notation bridge: 'dL/dh_(T-k) = (dL/dh_T) x w^k'. Use proper subscripts and exponents, a multiplication cross instead of the letter x, capital T for the ending, and k for the number of handoffs. Add the short key 'k = handoffs back; same w in every link'. Then three spacious horizontal cases with aligned columns headed '2 handoffs: expand the factors', '10 handoffs: plug into the power', '20 handoffs: plug into the power'. Each cell MUST show the full numerical substitution, not just its answer. Blue case labeled 'w = 0.8 | VANISHING': show '1 x 0.8 x 0.8 = 0.64', '1 x (0.8)^10 approx 0.11', and '1 x (0.8)^20 approx 0.012'. Caption 'Each link passes only 80%: distant feedback fades.' Muted green case labeled 'w = 1.0 | STEADY': show '1 x 1.0 x 1.0 = 1', '1 x (1.0)^10 = 1', and '1 x (1.0)^20 = 1'. Caption 'Each link preserves the message size on this linear route.' Restrained orange case labeled 'w = 1.2 | EXPLODING': show '1 x 1.2 x 1.2 = 1.44', '1 x (1.2)^10 approx 6.19', and '1 x (1.2)^20 approx 38.34'. Caption 'Each link boosts the current message by 20%: feedback grows.' Use proper mathematical approximation signs in place of the word approx. Circle the substituted 0.8, 1.0 and 1.2 factors lightly, so the relationship to w is immediately visible. No answer-only sequences, no bare arrows from small to large numbers. Footer, readable and succinct: 'One linear state route, not the full shared-weight gradient. Values are calculated and rounded, not training results.' Last line: 'Real tanh can also mute feedback; a large w alone does not guarantee explosion.' The complete formula with explicit substitutions is the teaching point, not decoration. No additional derivations, softmax/probability arrays, loss calculation or tiny dense type.
acceptance_criteria: 1536 by 1024 clean ruled notepad only. The shared backward-feedback formula is visible above the cases and includes a plain-English reading. All nine cells show the starting 1, the actual chosen weight substituted as repeated factors or a parenthesized power, and the correct result. Two-handoff gains are exactly 0.64, 1 and 1.44; ten-handoff gains round to 0.11, 1 and 6.19; twenty-handoff gains round to 0.012, 1 and 38.34. Superscripts are 10 and 20, not multiplied by 10 or 20. State-route versus shared-weight-gradient boundary and tanh caveat remain visible. Readable at notebook width, sparse one-line captions, no hands or external background.
prohibited_content: People, hands, thumbs, fingers, faces, arms, pens, desks, rooms, logos, watermarks, model/provider branding, answer-only progressions, missing substitutions, replacing powers with multiplication by the exponent, wrong decimal placement, omitted starting feedback, fabricated training results, probabilities or loss values, additional derivative chains, illegible cursive, or a claim that this is the entire shared-weight gradient or a universal nonlinear RNN rule.
alt_text: A handwritten notepad substitutes three weights into earlier feedback equals ending feedback times w to the power k. Starting from one, two handoffs show 1 times 0.8 times 0.8 equals 0.64, 1 times 1 times 1 equals 1, and 1 times 1.2 times 1.2 equals 1.44. The next columns explicitly substitute each weight into powers of ten and twenty, giving about 0.11 and 0.012, 1 and 1, or 6.19 and 38.34. Short captions explain fading, steady and growing feedback on a linear route, with the tanh caveat.
